definitions.meaning: the political left in Britain is the ... Party
a mother holds her newborn once childbirth is over

explanation.walkthrough: Every down clue in this puzzle opens with 'Left'. The Labour Party is Britain's main party of the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The main left-wing party in Britain carries this name, and it is also the word for childbirth.

indicators.note: the nurse is holding something within her arms, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a senior nurse is called a sister in British hospitals
hip means fashionable, in

explanation.surface: A nurse leaves, gripping a patient's hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for left-hand, and in heraldry the left side of a shield, as in bar sinister.

clue.text: Left Greens reversing round American city

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the abbreviation for left
the greens are turned back to front, read from right to left

parts.note: salad is a dish of greens

explanation.surface: Environmentalist left-wingers back-pedal around a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns SALAD into DALAS, and 'round' wraps that round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in Texas, USA.

indicators.note: the small and ducks pieces sit inside the toaster word

parts.note: a toasting fork is a long fork for toasting bread at a fire
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O, so ducks are OO

explanation.surface: Someone abandons little ducklings inside a toaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'toaster' here is the long fork used to hold bread to a fire. In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so two of them are OO.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsook is the past tense of forsake, meaning abandoned or left.

clue.text: Left with airtime to show picket line

parts.note: an air is a tune, as is an aria
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's airtime goes to covering a workers' picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airtime' splits into AIR (a tune, giving ARIA) and TIME (giving T). A 'picket line' here is a rope for tethering a grazing horse to a picket stake, not a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a rope used to tether a grazing animal to a stake, or a lasso.

indicators.note: the left piece comes after the TV piece

parts.note: tele is short for television
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: After walking out, someone appears on a television broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: teleporting sends a person as a signal, like a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Science-fiction teleporting transmits a body as a signal to a distant place, a whimsical kind of broadcasting.

indicators.note: in the surface the drug isn't working; the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Viagra failing to work for an airline pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator steers or pilots a ship or aircraft, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Left-handed first to provide a banger

indicators.note: the handed word is placed first, ahead of the left abbreviation

parts.note: handed means gave

explanation.surface: A left-handed batsman gets first chance to supply a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-handed' looks like one word but splits into L and 'handed' (GAVE), with 'first' putting GAVE ahead. A 'banger' is British slang for a sausage, here something that bangs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavel is the small hammer that a judge or auctioneer bangs, so it is literally a banger.

clue.text: Left politician (extremely cold one) with top celebrities

parts.note: extremely means so, as in so cold
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician, very aloof, rubs shoulders with the A-list.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialist is a politician of the left, supporting common ownership.

indicators.note: the letters are used to make a new word, a signal to rearrange them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lone person stays behind to make lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Filet is a kind of net lace with a square mesh.

indicators.note: the foot word holds the left letter inside it

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: A left foot gets stuck in a bowl of trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy or play with it, a verb synonym.

indicators.note: the animal is held inside the soldiers

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature caught by troops is set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived for without charge, so free of cost.

indicators.note: production means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A proposal to ban oil production.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblation is a religious offering made to a god.

indicators.note: the turned tree sits inside the earth

parts.note: clay is a kind of earth

indicators.note: a reflection shows the tree word back to front

parts.note: a fir is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree mirrored in the soil lights up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns the tree backwards to RIF; 'Illuminate' is the definition, not the light that does the reflecting.
explanation.definitionFit: To clarify is to make clear, to throw light on or illuminate a matter.

clue.text: Left boy to pen red pig

indicators.note: the boy encloses the other pieces as a pen holds animals

parts.note: a lad is a boy
R is an abbreviation for red
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A boy is left to keep a red pig in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old nautical word for the port, or left-hand, side of a ship.

clue.text: Left centre upset about commercial flag

indicators.note: the turned letters go around the commercial
in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, read backwards
the centre of the word left is its middle two letters

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A centre-left politician is angry about a TV advert and its flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes the middle two letters of LEFT, which 'upset' turns to FE. 'flag' is a verb meaning droop, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or weaken, the same sense as to fade.

indicators.note: something explosive blows apart, so the word is blown into a new order

explanation.surface: A naval term for smart and trim, used of something that could go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' rearranges TIDDLEY. Tiddley is a naval slang word for smart, also spelt tiddly, meaning tipsy, which suits a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyddite is a high explosive made from picric acid, named after Lydd in Kent.

clue.text: Left for dead in Glasgow boxing neighbourhood

indicators.note: the Scots word is packed round the neighbourhood as a box holds contents

parts.note: deed is the Scots form of dead
a part is a district, as in these parts

explanation.surface: Left for dead after a boxing match in a Glasgow district.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow is in Scotland, where 'deed' is a dialect form of dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is the past tense of depart, meaning went away or left.

indicators.note: the left word sits outside the many letter

parts.note: exited means left
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Left out in the cold, many people get worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited and overwrought both describe someone in an agitated, worked-up state.

clue.text: Established when hot rod crashed into farm animal

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the farm animal

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal

indicators.note: a crashed hot rod is wrecked, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A conventional story: a hot rod smashed into a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' scrambles the hot rod's letters to RTHODO; the surface's car smash hides a simple container.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means conforming to established, accepted beliefs or practice.

clue.text: Left to change top with some relief

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is changed for another

parts.note: willed means left, as by a will

explanation.surface: Someone left a mind changed, with a sense of relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' as in bequeathed in a will gives WILLED; 'to change top' swaps its first letter. Relief here is raised land.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilled land has some hills, and relief is the variation in a landscape's height.

parts.note: people who have quit their homeland and now live abroad

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the theme's political word but simply means they left home.
explanation.definitionFit: Expatriates are citizens who have moved away and settled in a foreign country.

clue.text: Left back to stable horse — say Winter Warmer

indicators.note: the turned word houses the horse as a stable does
the left word is read backwards

parts.note: gone means left
gee-gee is a childish name for a horse, said as G G

explanation.surface: A rider leaves, returning to stable a horse with a winter hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the left word to ENOG; 'stable' is a verb, to house a horse, not the steady adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a rich drink of eggs, milk and spirit, drunk hot in winter.

clue.text: Left with time up front, then you're first to score

indicators.note: the time letter is placed at the front, before the left word

parts.note: went means left

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of you're

explanation.surface: A player leaves early, then you're the first one to score.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, an old counting unit for that number.

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
ult is short for ultimo, last month

explanation.surface: Coming second to last by a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' is a verb, not the garden building.
explanation.definitionFit: To moult is to shed feathers, hair or skin.

indicators.note: damage breaks the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Inflexible charges are harming an opera company.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried is the third opera in Wagner's Ring cycle.

indicators.note: the phrase supplies, provides, the letters within it

explanation.surface: Bringing routine medical supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplies' points to the run inside 'regular medical'.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed means carrying a weapon.

clue.text: Vice unit given odd notes by witnesses

parts.note: a vice-president is a deputy, DEP for short
one is a unit

indicators.note: the odd letters of notes, first, third and fifth, are kept

explanation.surface: A vice squad gets strange notes from witnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Deponents are people who give sworn evidence, which is what witnesses do.
